title: Import map
description: How an import's source entities become actors of this atlas. It is not a record: nothing under data/imports/ is a node of the graph, it carries no provenance envelope, and the browser never reads it. It exists so that correcting which actor a territory belongs to is one entry in one JSON file through the ordinary pull-request path, and a maintainer re-running the import — never a hand-edited presence. tools/validate.mjs checks it; whether a code exists in the source is checked at import time, loudly.

source.description: The id of the source record the import cites, so a map cannot be pointed at the wrong dataset by accident.

entries.description: Keyed by the source's own entity code — for CShapes the Gleditsch–Ward code, so an entity renamed in the data still lands on the right record. A code absent from here gets the actor the import derives from the entity's name, and --report lists it.

actor.description: The actor the code's territory belongs to, or — with splits — the actor of the first segment. Created by the import when no record of that id exists, reused untouched when one does.

names.description: The names to give an actor the import creates, when the source's own name for the code is wrong for the segment — CShapes calls entity 750 "India" from 1886, colony and republic alike. names[0] is the display name. Ignored for an actor that already exists.

note.description: Why the mapping is what it is, for whoever reads the file next.

splits.description: Where one source code is more than one actor. Each split cuts the code's features by date, in order: the first segment belongs to the entry's own actor, and every feature starting on or after a split's date belongs to that split's actor until the next one. A date must fall on a boundary the source itself draws — the day after some feature's end — or the import errors and names the nearest ones.

from.description: ISO date, the first day of the new actor's segment. Strictly increasing across an entry's splits.
